rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fresh pasture vegetation dries and rots into black refuse like manure and coal.
rows.anchor: mer‘alarda ter ü taze çıkan nebâtâtın bir müddet sonra kuruyup çürüyerek gübre ve kömür gibi kara bir gusâya çevrildiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A detailed view sees mineral coal as plants that died and decomposed under water; the phrase also points to this origin.
rows.anchor: bütün maden kömürlerinin dahi mâhiyeti nebâtâtın sular içinde ölüp tehallül ederek çevrildiği kara bir gusâdan ibaret olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's vegetation and its transformation into black refuse display God's creation, ordering, measure, and transformation as Lord.
rows.anchor: Bütün bunlar O’nun halk u tesviyesi, takdir ü tahvîli ile rubûbiyetinin eseridir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who reduce humanity to bodily, plant-like, and animal aims end like combustible black coal refuse.
rows.anchor: insanlığı sırf nebâtî ve hayvânî surette sade bedenî gayelerle anlamak isteyen bedbahtların âkıbetleri de böyle kara bir gusâdan ibaret olan maden kömürleri gibi kābil-i ihtirak olmaktan başka bir şey değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warning people about this fate is an additional guidance by which the Most High Lord makes himself known to humanity, especially through the Prophet's particular guidance.
rows.anchor: bilhassa Resûlullah’a olan hidâyet-i mahsûsasını beyan ve tefhim için buyuruluyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every outward and hidden state of people, so his promise to teach and preserve revelation is grounded in complete knowledge and merits trust and glorification.
rows.anchor: Şüphesiz ki O, Allah, cehri de bilir gizliyi de her şeyden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse means God knows what is recited aloud and secretly; the Prophet should recite openly or privately as appropriate and act without forgetting.
rows.anchor: yüksek sesle okunanı da bilir, gizli okunanı da.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is parenthetical and is also grammatically attached to the promise that the Prophet will be made to recite.
rows.anchor: Bu cümle mu‘terizadır. Şu da سَنُقْرِئُكَ’ye ma‘tuftur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will make the Prophet successful in the easiest path or goal and turn this success into an easy, firmly rooted disposition.
rows.anchor: Ve seni yüsrâya müyesser, yani muvaffak kılacağız. Her hususta en kolay yola veya gayeye erdireceğiz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This facilitation covers every religious domain: knowledge, teaching, practice, guidance, and finding guidance; the Prophet and his religion reach the hardest ends with ease.
rows.anchor: dinin her bâbında: ilimde, tâlimde, amelde, hidâyet ve ihtidâda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise includes receiving outward and inward revelation and the ease of a generous, unburdensome law that perfects the self and others.
rows.anchor: zâhir ve bâtından vahiy telakkīsini ve ondaki semâhatli ve harecsiz şeriat ve ahkâmın gerek tekmîl-i nefse ve gerek tekmîl-i gayra müte‘allik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawhid, sincerity, true knowledge, and rightly ordered effort are foundations of ease, whose foremost source is God's enabling grace.
rows.anchor: Îmân-ı tevhid, ihlâs, ilm-i hak, usûlüyle sa‘y ü amel her kolaylığın başı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to teach and communicate the rules and knowledge contained in revelation, admonish people, and make them reflect.
rows.anchor: ahkâm ve ma‘ârifi halka tâlim ve tebliğ ile va‘z u nasihat et, öğüt ver, düşündür

rows.speaker: Müfessirîn
rows.claim: Exegetes say the condition that reminder benefit is not restrictive: it emphasizes the command and, to a degree, eases it.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn demişlerdir ki: Resûlullah mutlaka tezkir ile me’mur olduğundan bu şart, esas itibariyle takyid için değil, tekid ve bir dereceye kadar tahfif içindir.

rows.speaker: Müfessirîn
rows.claim: The condition emphasizes certainty because eloquent admonition always offers some benefit; whether listeners want to benefit is a separate matter.
rows.anchor: haddizâtında beliğ olan bir tezkir muhatablar hakkında bir menfaat ifade etmekten hâlî olmaz. Muhatabların ondan intifâ‘etmek isteyip istememeleri ise diğer bir şeydir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's compassion, patience through harm, and intense desire for his people’s salvation explain why the conditional wording also relieves him; the cited passages describe these qualities.
rows.anchor: nâsa acıyor, kavminin imana gelerek saadete ermelerine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When admonition demonstrably brings harm rather than benefit by intensifying rebellion, it is not obligatory to continue and turning away may be preferable.
rows.anchor: olmayıp da zarar melhuz olan husûsâtta tezkir vâcib kılınmayıp terkine ruhsat bulunduğuna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If some benefit is reasonably expected, admonition remains incumbent, with attention to those who will listen and take heed.
rows.anchor: asl olduğu üzere az çok bir fâide melhuz bulunursa dinleyip istifade edecek olanları nazar-ı mülâhazaya alarak vaaz etmek ehline vâcib olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reverent person will remember and accept counsel, while the most wretched person will avoid it.
rows.anchor: En bedbaht olan da kaçınacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched person leans into the greatest fire, the everlasting fire of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: en büyük ateşe, yani âhirette ebedî olan cehennem ateşine yaslanacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In hell he neither dies to escape torment nor has a life with pleasure or benefit that would make endurance meaningful; this is unsurpassable misery.
rows.anchor: Ölmez ki dünya azâbından kurtulduğu gibi kurtulsun, hayat yani zevk ve menfaati olan bir hayat da bulmaz ki çektiği azâbı ona vesile addederek sabr u tahammül etsin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This fate is much worse than pasture turning to black coal refuse, and explains the outcome of those who shun admonition.
rows.anchor: mer‘aların kara bir gusâ olan kömüre çevrilmesinden çok büyük bir bedbahtlıktır. Ve işte va‘z u nasihat dinlemekten kaçınanların âkıbeti de budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes hold that never dying in hell applies to disbelievers; sinful believers who enter it die, based on Muslim's report from Abu Sa'id.
rows.anchor: Demişlerdir ki cehennemde ölmemek kâfirlere mahsustur. Amma usât-ı mü’minînden cehenneme girenler orada öleceklerdir. Buna Müslim’in Ebû Sa‘îd’den rivayet ettiği şu hadis ile istidlâl eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd
rows.claim: The report says hell's permanent inhabitants neither die nor live, but God kills sinful people touched by the fire; after they become charcoal, intercession brings them to Paradise, where they grow when watered.
rows.anchor: Buna Müslim’in Ebû Sa‘îd’den rivayet ettiği şu hadis ile istidlâl eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For disbelievers, not dying or living follows the two deaths and two lives mentioned in 40:11, after resurrection for punishment.
rows.anchor: iki hayat ile azab için ba‘s olunduktan sonra demektir ki

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Others take the wording about neither dying nor living as a metaphor for enduring misery under the severity of torment.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da demişlerdir ki “ne ölmek ne de dirilmek” tâbiri şiddet-i azâb ile ebedî sürünmekten kinayedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success means escaping evil and attaining one's aim; purification includes taking admonition, cleansing the heart of shirk and bad character, and the body of physical and spiritual impurity.
rows.anchor: Kendini fenalıklardan kurtarıp murâda erdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification also includes faith, sincerity, ritual washing and ablution, and giving zakat to seek standing purified before God.
rows.anchor: bedenini maddî ve mânevî pisliklerden temizleyip iman ve ihlâs ve gusül ve abdest ile paklanan ve zekâtını verip huzûr-ı ilâhîde temize çıkmak için çalışan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering the Lord's name means recalling that one will stand before him, beginning prayer with the takbir Allahu akbar.
rows.anchor: Rabbinin ismini anıp O’nun huzûruna varacağını düşünerek “Allahu ekber” diye tekbir alıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer includes the five daily prayers and, according to a transmitted report, especially the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: namaz kılan beş vakit namazı ve bâhusus vârid olan rivayete göre bayram namazını kılan kimseler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense points to inner and bodily purification, self-discipline, tawhid and verbal takbir, and obligatory zakat and prayer as foundations of bodily and financial worship.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetin zâhiri kalb ve beden temizliğiyle terbiye-i nefse, tevhid, tekbir gibi zikr-i lisâna

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Some authorities, including Ibn al-Mundhir, transmit Ibn Abbas's interpretation in line with the verse's apparent broad sense.
rows.anchor: İbn Münzir gibi bazılarının İbn Abbas’tan rivayetleri de böyledir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some authorities say the unrestricted wording includes voluntary acts as well as obligations, since its generality should ordinarily remain in force.
rows.anchor: Bazıları farzlarla beraber mümkin olduğu kadar nevâfile de şümûlünü söylemişlerdir. Çünkü mutlaktır, ıtlâkı üzere cereyanı asıldır.

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Ibn Masud invoked a prayer for God's mercy on a person who gives charity and performs prayer.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan: رَحِمَ اللهُ امْرَأً تَصَدَّقَ وَصَلَّى

rows.speaker: İkrime, Ebu’l-Âliye, İbn Sîrîn, İbn Ömer
rows.claim: A group interprets purification as paying the fitra charity before Eid and remembrance-prayer as takbir followed by Eid prayer, implying obligation for both Eid prayer and fitra.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin beyânına göre bu tefsir İkrime’nin, Ebu’l-Âliye’nin, İbn Sîrîn’in, İbn Ömer’in kavilleridir.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The fitra-and-Eid interpretation is also reported as a Prophetic narration.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’a merfû‘an da rivayet edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: Ali identifies purification with paying fitra and says the verses suffice to describe giving it, going to the prayer ground, pronouncing the opening takbir, and performing Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali kerremallâhu vechehu’dan dahi şöyle mervîdir: “Bu tezekkî sadaka-i fıtr ile tasadduktur”

rows.speaker: Dahhâk
rows.claim: Dahhak explains the remembrance as reciting takbir on the way to the prayer ground before performing Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: Dahhâk’tan rivayette de وَذَكَرَ ٱسْمَ رَبِّهِۦ فَصَلَّىٰ “musallâya giderken Rabbinin ismini zikredip, yani tekbir alarak gidip de bayram namazı kılan” diye mervîdir.

rows.speaker: Sa‘lebî
rows.claim: Sa'labi objects that the sura is unanimously Meccan, while neither financial zakat nor Eid existed in Mecca.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki Mekke’de ne mâlî zekât ne de îd yoktu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reply says the sura could have been revealed in Mecca in preparation while its ruling took effect later; Meccan classification is more correct but not unanimous, since some call it Medinan.
rows.anchor: bu Mekke’de ihzârî surette nâzil olup hükmü teahhur etmiş olabilir. Bir de sûrenin Mekkî olması esah ise de icmâ‘î değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither prayer nor purification should be restricted to Eid prayer or financial zakat, even if these were an occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: buradaki namazı, sebeb-i nüzûl bile olsa yalnız bayram namazına hasretmek lâzım gelmeyeceği gibi, tezekkîyi de yalnız zekât-ı mâlîye ve o meyanda bilhassa sadaka-i fıtra tahsis lâzım gelmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification is general inner and outward cleansing and growth in deeds and wealth; prayer broadly includes the five daily prayers and obligatory Eid and witr prayers.
rows.anchor: “Tezekkî” bâtınî, zâhirî temizlik ve tefeyyüz mânasıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruling could be practiced in Mecca as far as possible, then in Medina with financial zakat, fitra, and Eid prayer; some applications took effect later rather than all at once.
rows.anchor: Medine’de de zekât-ı mâlî ve fitre ve bayram namazı dahi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports naming fitra and Eid prayer mean these rites are included in the verse, not that they exhaust its meaning; voluntary acts also fit its unrestricted wording.
rows.anchor: sadaka-i fıtrı ve bayram namazını söyleyenlerin murâdı da hasr değil, bunların dahi bu âyet hükmünde dâhil bulunduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification, remembrance, and prayer are roots pointing to all inward, verbal, financial, and bodily acts of worship.
rows.anchor: tezekkî ve zikir ve salâtın zikri de kalbî ve lisânî, mâlî ve bedenî bi’l-cümle ibâdâtın aslı olmak itibariyle hepsine işaret olması dahi sahih ve mervîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead of striving for purification and success, heedless people prefer worldly adornment, amusement, food, drink, women, pleasures, and spending wealth on them.
rows.anchor: dünyâ hayâtı tercih ediyorsunuz onun ziynetini, eğlencesini, yemesini, içmesini, kadınlarını, lezzetlerini takdim ediyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At festivals they enjoy passing worldly pleasures more than purifying themselves, giving charity, remembering God, praying, and doing lasting good.
rows.anchor: Bayram yapmak istediğiniz vakit de temizlik, tasadduk, zikir, namaz, hayr u hasenât gibi sonu felah olan amellerden ziyade gelip geçici dünya lezzetlerinden zevk alıyorsunuz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One kind of worldly preference belongs to disbelievers who desire no meeting with God and settle contentedly for this life; cited verses describe their abode and lack of afterlife share.
rows.anchor: likāullâhı arzu etmeyip sade dünyâ hayâta râzı ve mutmain olan ve ibadet etseler bile yalnız رَبَّنَٓا اٰتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا diyenlerin hâlidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second kind consists of heedless or sinful believers who ask for good in both lives but sacrifice the afterlife when the two interests conflict; their share depends on their deeds.
rows.anchor: demekle beraber te‘âruz hâlinde dünyayı âhirete tercih edenler, dünya zevki için âhıreti feda eyleyen gāfil veya âsî mü’minlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the afterlife is better and more enduring, intelligent people should choose it and work for purification and success; worldly preference inevitably ends in loss.
rows.anchor: âhiret daha hayırlı ve daha devamlıdır. Binâen‘aleyh fâni olan dünyâ hayat ne kadar zevkli olursa olsun âkil ve zeki olan insanların âhireti tercih ederek tezekkî ve felâha çalışmaları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who choose the afterlife may endure worldly hardship without despair; their aim is to escape worldly pains and reach God's pleasure, not merely remain alive.
rows.anchor: dünyada ne kadar mihnet ve ıztırab görseler âkıbetten bedbin olmaz, ye’se düşmez, günden güne felah ve saadete doğru gitmeye ve hüsn-i hâtimeye muvaffak olurlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife-oriented person gives the obligatory charity, remembers the Lord, and prays in preparation to meet him.
rows.anchor: başının vergisini verip Rabbinin ismini anarak O’na gitmek üzere namazını kılan, ibadetini yapan kimseler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word this may refer to the reminder that the afterlife is better, the report of success through purification, or the whole sura and the promised success of Muhammad's mission through Qur'anic revelation, recitation, preservation, and facilitation.
rows.anchor: bu tezkir, âhiretin dünyadan hayırlı ve devamlı olması ihtârı, yahut قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ ihbârı veya bu sûre mazmûnu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The central teachings of Islam here are already stated and promised in earlier scriptures, especially Abraham's and Moses's: tawhid, divine transcendence, recitation and admonition, reverence, purification, remembrance, prayer, and the superiority of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Rabb-i A‘lâ’yı tevhid ve tenzih, okumak, va‘z u tezkir, saygı, tezekkî ve zikr u salât ile felah, âhiretin dünyadan hayırlı ve bekālı olması esasları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk, trinitarianism, anthropomorphism, and preferring the world over the afterlife are false doctrines; despite opposition, Muhammad's mission and true religion will prevail.
rows.anchor: din nâmına buna muhalif olan şirk, teslis ve teşbih ve dünyayı âhirete tercih gibi bedbin fikirler, akideler doğru değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised emergence of the true religion follows from the mission's facilitation, as also stated in the verses promising the Messenger's victory with guidance and the true religion.
rows.anchor: risâlet-i Muhammediyenin ve bu dîn-i hakkın yüsrâya muvaffakiyeti bütün bunların bir neticesi olmak üzere emr-i muhakkaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa, meaning books or pages; beyond the four major scriptures, it commonly names revealed epistles sent to prophets.
rows.anchor: kitap mânasına “sahîfe”nin cem‘i olup Tevrat, Zebur, İncil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is transmitted that Moses received ten scrolls before the Torah and Abraham also received ten scrolls.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’nın suhufu Tevrat’tan evvel indirilmiş olan on suhuf, İbrâhim’inki de on suhuf idi diye nakledilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Zer
rows.claim: A report says God sent 104 books: 50 scrolls to Seth, 30 to Idris, 10 each to Abraham and Moses before the Torah, then the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Criterion.
rows.anchor: Abd b. Humeyd ve İbn Merdûye ve İbn Asâkir Ebû Zer radıyallahu anh’tan rivayet etmişlerdir: “Dedim ki: ‘Yâ Resûlallah, Allah teâlâ kaç kitap indirdi?’

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: In the report, Abraham's scrolls teach that rulers are sent to defend the oppressed, and God does not reject an oppressed person's prayer even when that person is an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: Ey o mübtelâya tasallut eden mağrur melik, ben seni dünyayı birbirine yığasın diye göndermedim, velâkin mazlûmun duasını Benden reddedesin diye gönderdim

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Abraham's scrolls advise a wise person to devote three periods to communion with God, self-examination and reflection, and lawful personal needs, which restores focus for the other periods.
rows.anchor: aklına karşı mağlub olmadıkça âkile gerektir ki üç saati ola: Bir saatinde Rabbine münâcat ede ve bir saatinde nefsini muhasebe ede

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The scrolls say the wise person should perceive the times, attend to his affairs, and guard his tongue; whoever counts speech as action speaks little except about meaningful matters.
rows.anchor: Âkile zamanına basîr, şe’nine mukbil, lisânına hâfız olmak gerektir.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A wise person should seek sound livelihood, preparation for the afterlife, and lawful enjoyment.
rows.anchor: Âkil üç şeyi tâlib olmak gerektir: Maîşetini ıslah veya me‘âdına hazırlık veya haramda olmayarak telezzüz.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Moses's scrolls call it astonishing that someone certain of death rejoices, certain of the Fire laughs, sees the world's changes yet remains attached to it, knows destiny yet grows angry, and knows reckoning yet does not act.
rows.anchor: Taaccüb ederim ölüme yakīni olup da sevinene, ateşe yakīni olup da gülene. Dünyayı ve ehline olan tekallübâtını görüp de ona gönül bağlayana

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Asked whether anything from Abraham's and Moses's scrolls was revealed to him, the Prophet answers yes and recites the verses on purification, prayer, worldly preference, and the better, enduring afterlife.
rows.anchor: Evet yâ Ebâ Zer قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ وَذَكَرَ ٱسْمَ رَبِّهِۦ فَصَلَّىٰ بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi says the report's authenticity is known to God, expressing uncertainty about its soundness.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh Âlûsî’nin dediği gibi hadîsin sıhhatini Allah bilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following Ghashiya sura continues the admonition by detailing the afterlife states of the damned and the successful.
rows.anchor: âhirette ateşe yaslanacak bedbahtlarla felah bulacak mes‘udların hâllerini tafsil ederek tezkîre devam olunmak üzere Sûre-i Gāşiye gelecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is rhetorical, urging attentive listening and affirming the importance of what follows.
rows.anchor: Bu istifham ehemmiyetle dinlemeye teşvik ve takrir içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghashiya derives from a verb meaning to cover from every side; it denotes an enveloping, widespread thing, with its feminine ending indicating grammatical femininity, intensification, or nominalization from an adjective.
rows.anchor: bir şeyi her tarafından sarıp bürüyen salgın, sargın, müstevlî şey demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root is used for a saddle covering, the membrane of the heart, an enveloping illness or nightmare, and an overwhelming calamity; 12:107 illustrates the last sense.
rows.anchor: At eğerinin örtüsüne ve kalb zarına ve insanı veya hayvanı içinden saran derde ve kâbus gibi her taraftan saran salgın müstevlî belâya ıtlak olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the definite article, al-Ghashiya is a name for the Resurrection because its terror suddenly surrounds people and all events.
rows.anchor: bu mânadan lâm ile ٱلْغَٰشِيَةِ de kıyametin isimlerindendir. Çünkü birdenbire şiddetiyle halkı saracak ve ehvâli, umûmu bürüyecektir.

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some say al-Ghashiya is the fire that will cover the faces of the disbelievers and people of Hell, as in 14:50; the majority prefers the Resurrection meaning because it fits the sura's flow.
rows.anchor: kâfirlerin, ashâb-ı nârın yüzlerini saracak olan nârdır

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Another reported view calls those who fall into and surround the fire the people of Hell; the majority prefers the preceding interpretation as more consistent with the sura's flow.
rows.anchor: düşüp onu saracak olan ehl-i nârdır demişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadith means a report passed from person to person and narrated as a story, worthy of being heard afresh each time; this report deserves lasting attention.
rows.anchor: her söylenişinde taze gibi dinlenmeye lâyık söz ve haber demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that enveloping Day, many faces are humbled: people who once failed to honor truth bow in fear and disgrace.
rows.anchor: o gün havf u haşyetle boynunu bükmüş, zillete düşmüştür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned are now laboring amid crushing deeds and hardship, or they labored in the past but their work brought only futile toil.
rows.anchor: Yahut vaktiyle çalışmamış, amel etmemiş değiller, çalışmışlar, amel yapmışlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their past work did not serve God or follow a true path; it followed false religion and corrupt belief, so they now suffer its penalty.
rows.anchor: bâtıl din, bozuk fikir ve itikad ile küfre saparak çalışmışlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, amilatun and nasibatun may be second and third predicates, or nasiba may function as an adjective; interpretations vary with whether they are restricted to that day.
rows.anchor: ikinci ve üçüncü haberdir. Yahut “nâsıbe” sıfattır.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: One reading restricts both descriptions to that day: people formerly not working on God's path are now bent under exhausting labor in humiliation, dragging chains and stocks through Hell.
rows.anchor: Bu mâna İbn Abbas’tan menkuldür.

rows.speaker: Zeyd b. Eslem
rows.claim: A second reading takes amilatun and nasibatun as worldly past: they performed work and worship, but unbelief and a false path nullified it, leaving futile exertion and present humiliation.
rows.anchor: Zeyd b. Eslem’den mervî olan bu mâna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author and many others prefer the worldly-work reading because the afterlife is the place of recompense, not labor; it also points to ascetics and monks whose intense worship follows error.
rows.anchor: Âhiret dârü’l-amel olmayıp dârü’l-cezâ olmak itibariyle amelin dünyada olması daha zâhir olduğundan birçokları bu mânayı tercih etmişler

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Bukhari records Ibn Abbas glossing the descriptions as referring to Christians.
rows.anchor: Buhârî’de قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ

rows.speaker: İkrime
rows.claim: Ikrima says amila refers to worldly activity and nasiba to suffering in the afterlife; the participles convey past work and continuing present or future toil, a plausible distinction between deeds and recompense.
rows.anchor: İkrime’den mervî olandır ki “âmile” dünyada

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These people lean against an intensely hot fire and are made to drink from a spring of boiling, fiery water.
rows.anchor: yüksek derece-i harârette şiddetli kızışgın bir ateşe gerilip yaslanırlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since zaqqum and gislīn have appeared elsewhere, some identify dari with either of them as a tree from fire, though the exclusive wording could describe distinct foods for different groups.
rows.anchor: gıslîn veya zakkum ile aynı şey olmak üzere

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan is reported by Razi as deriving dari from a causative sense: a harsh, bitter, burning thing that forces those who eat it into abasement and pleading.
rows.anchor: Tefsîr-i Râzî’de Hasan’dan bir rivayette

rows.speaker: ekser müfessirîn
rows.claim: Most commentators say dari is dried shibrik, a thorn that camels eat when fresh but avoid when dry, and a deadly poison.
rows.anchor: şibrıkın kurusudur. “Şibrık” bir nevi dikendir ki yaş iken onu deve yer

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says Arabs call the plant shibrik when fresh and dari when dry in the Hijaz, while other Arabs call it shibrik; it is poisonous.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr der ki: “Arabda ‘darî‘’

rows.speaker: İkrime
rows.claim: Ikrima says Quraysh called the low thorny plant shibrik in spring and dari when it dried into a stalk.
rows.anchor: İkrime’den rivayetinde: Yere yapışık dikenli bir ağaçtır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan cites dari as shibrik, a poor pasture on which grazing animals gain neither fat nor flesh; a Hudhali poet's line is evidence for this usage.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân’ın nakillerine göre darî‘şibrıktır ki fena bir mer‘adır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Hudhali verse depicts animals confined among dry dari thorn, witnessing its use for the plant's dry, difficult growth.
rows.anchor: وَحُبِسْنَ فيِ هَزْمِ الضَّرِيعِ فَكُلُّهَا حَدْبَاءُ دَامِيَةُ الْيَدَيْنِ حَرُودُ

rows.speaker: Ebû Züeyb
rows.claim: Abu Dhu'ayb's poem says animals grazed lush shibrik but left when it shriveled into dari, becoming lean; it witnesses the plant's change when dried.
rows.anchor: Ebû Züeyb de şöyle demiştir.

rows.speaker: بعض لغويين
rows.claim: Some lexicographers call dari the crumbs of dried arfej.
rows.anchor: Bazı lügaviyyîn, arfec kurusunun kırıntısı

rows.speaker: Zeccâc
rows.claim: Zajjaj identifies dari as a plant like avsec.
rows.anchor: Zeccâc avsec gibi bir ot demiş

rows.speaker: Halil
rows.claim: Khalil calls it a green, extremely foul-smelling plant cast up by the sea.
rows.anchor: Halil de yeşil ve gayet

rows.speaker: Kāmûs
rows.claim: The Qamus adds meanings including date-palm thorn, a plant in turbid rotten water, and an aquatic plant whose roots do not reach earth.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs’ta bu mânalardan başka hurma ağacının dikenine ve bulanık müte‘affin sularda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dari can name several inedible thorny, hard or foul-smelling poisonous plants; the point is their painful and impossible-to-eat quality, echoed in the description that they do not nourish or relieve hunger.
rows.anchor: Arapça’da “darî‘” insanın değil hayvanın bile yemesi kābil olmayan dikenli, sert veya yumuşak olsa da gayet fena kokulu zehir zenberek birkaç türlü dikene ve nebâta ıtlak olunurmuş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word also suggests hurting through abasement; the phrase about no nourishment clarifies that this is an inedible torment.
rows.anchor: bir darâ‘at ve zillet ile sızlandırmak mefhûmunu îmâ eden “darî‘” lafzıyla ifade edilmiş

rows.speaker: Sa‘îd
rows.claim: Some exegetes transmitted from Said interpret dari as stones.
rows.anchor: Sa‘îd’den rivayet olunduğu üzere bazı müfessirîn bunu taş diye tefsir etmiş

rows.speaker: İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says worldly dari is a dry leafless thorn, while in the afterlife it is a thorn made of fire.
rows.anchor: İbn Zeyd’den de şöyle rivayet edilmiştir: Dünyada darî‘, Arabın “darî‘” dediği yapraksız kuru dikendir. Âhirette darî‘de ateşten bir dikendir.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets dari as a tree of fire.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayette: Ateşten bir ağaçtır.

rows.speaker: Kāmûs
rows.claim: The Qamus reports another view: in Hell it is more bitter than aloe, fouler-smelling than carrion, and hotter than fire.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs’ta alâ kavlin: Cehennemde acı sabırdan acı, lâşeden daha bed kokulu ve ateşten daha yakıcı bir şeydir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is compulsory eating of something impossible to swallow; zaqqum, gislīn, and dari each clarify the choking food of 73:13, yet even forced eating neither nourishes nor relieves hunger.
rows.anchor: “zakkum”, “gıslîn”, “darî‘” hepsi Sûre-i Müzzemmil’deki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These images help people infer the unimaginable bitterness of afterlife punishment from the suffering of famine, calamity, and enslavement experienced in this world.
rows.anchor: dünyada büyük açlık ve felâket, esaret hengâmlarında gördükleri âlâm ve ıztırâbâttan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In contrast, other faces are gentle and blessed, enjoying felicity.
rows.anchor: birtakım yüzler de o gün

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naima may derive from softness and mean a gentle, soft face showing the joy of blessing, or from blessing and mean immersed in bliss; both readings indicate happiness.
rows.anchor: “Nâ‘ime” letâfet mânasına “nu‘ûmet”ten

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed are pleased with their effort because it was not wasted: it followed God's command and approval, was accepted, and bore fruit on the terrifying Day, spurring further effort.
rows.anchor: Çünkü boşuna çalışmamışlar, amelleri Allah’ın emr ü rızâsına muvâfık yolda cereyan eylemiş, kabule iktiran etmiş, sa‘yleri o dehşetli günde semeresini vermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their Garden is high both in physical location and in rank.
rows.anchor: Hem mekânen hem mekâneten yüksek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean that no idle word, foolish speech, or group occupied with futility is heard there, or it may address the listener directly.
rows.anchor: bir lâğıye, yani lağv veya boş bir kelime

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghiya has three analyses: a laghiya word, a group of futile speakers, or a verbal noun like aqiba meaning idle speech itself.
rows.anchor: yahut lağv mânasına “âkıbet” gibi masdar olmak üzere üç kavil vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghv means useless, meaningless speech or actions that should be discarded, broadly including futile words and deeds; laghiya can specifically mean gross error or cursing.
rows.anchor: “Lağv” de “lâğıye” mânasına olarak ilgā ve ıskātı gerek olan, ehemmiyet verilecek bir fâidesi olmayan boş, mânasız, herze, heder, beyhûde şeylere ıtlak olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran says the Garden contains neither idle speech nor falsehood.
rows.anchor: Cennette bunlar işitilmez لَّا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًۭا وَلَا كِذَّٰبًۭا’dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning freedom from frivolity first signals the Garden's purity and its inhabitants' refinement, correcting worldly assumptions that luxury requires entertainment, gossip, or shameless chatter.
rows.anchor: cennetin ve ehl-i cennetin nezâhetini iş‘âr ile mü’minleri ahlâk-ı fâzılaya tergībdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should turn away from frivolity as in 23:3, increasingly avoid it in prosperity as well as hardship, and desire blessings unlike those that ruin the ignorant.
rows.anchor: diye tasrih olunduğu üzere bu ahlâk ile mütehallık olmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description gives spiritual qualities priority over bodily delights: satisfaction with one's effort is among the highest pleasures and a pleasure that brings a person to the station of praise.
rows.anchor: sa‘ye rızâ: sa‘yinden hoşnutluk, insanı makām-ı hamde erdiren lezzetlerin en yükseğidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Effort is the only thing a person has, as stated in 53:39 and 2:286; life's true enjoyment lies in effort directed toward its goal, and success in that goal gives effort its pleasure.
rows.anchor: Hayat, haddizâtında faaliyet demek olduğu için hakikatte zevk-i hayat, gayesine masruf olan sa‘y zevkinden ibarettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Effort that misses its goal ends in exhaustion and disappointment like the damned in 88:3, while purposeless or trivial effort is itself frivolity; these contrasts explain the Garden's two spiritual qualities.
rows.anchor: Gayesine isabet etmeyen sa‘y ve amel sonunda عَامِلَةٌۭ نَّاصِبَةٌۭ hükmünce nasab ve te‘ab ve inkisâr-ı hayâl ile elem ü hüsrandan ibaret kalacağı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden has a flowing spring that can run wherever desired and spreads life's source and animation; other passages mention multiple springs, so the singular is generic or points to the most universal spring.
rows.anchor: o cennette akan bir menba istenilen yere cereyan eden bir kaynak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spring's indefinite form magnifies it rather than making it singular, and marks it as unknown and beyond anything a human has seen, heard, or imagined.
rows.anchor: Tenkîri de mâruf olan menbalardan olmayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised couches are thrones, chairs, beds, or palace-like seats; their elevation may be physical height or elevated honor.
rows.anchor: veya yatılan karyola ve köşk kabîlinden şeylere ıtlak olunur; rif‘ati de zeminden yüksekliği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The handleless cups and pitchers are placed nearby, ready for drinking; 76:5-6 similarly describes the righteous drinking from a cup.
rows.anchor: Küpler kulpu olmayan küp, sürahi, bardak gibi meşrubat kapları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Namariq are cushions lined up for leaning on; the initial nun may carry a damma or kasra.
rows.anchor: nûn’un zammı veya kesri ile نمرقه dayanmak için konulan koltuk yastığı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarabi are spread or scattered fine, splendid rugs; Qamus also applies the word to plants that yellow and redden while retaining green, and says rugs may be named by comparison with them.
rows.anchor: “zerâbiyy” sararmış ve kızarmış olmakla beraber yeşilliği de bulunan otlara dahi denir

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib says zarabiyy originally meant speckled textiles associated with a place, then became a metaphor for rugs.
rows.anchor: Râgıb demiştir ki: “Zerâbiyy” fi’l-asl bir mevzi‘e mensub benekli dokumalardır. Sonra döşemelere istiare olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: Ferrâ
rows.claim: Farra describes the rugs as fine-pile carpets.
rows.anchor: Ferrâ’nın beyânına göre ince tüylü halılardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some dictionaries treat cushions and rugs as interchangeable, while Jawhari distinguishes them; Hind's rajaz uses namariq for rugs, since people do not walk on pillows.
rows.anchor: Tanâfisle himl-i rakīk, nemârik ve zerâbî yekdiğeri makāmında da kullanıldığından Sıhâh-ı Cevherî aralarını ayırmıştır.

rows.speaker: Hind
rows.claim: Hind's rajaz uses namariq to mean rugs; the author infers this because one does not normally walk on cushions.
rows.anchor: Hind’in: نَحْنُ بَنَاتُ طَارِق نَمْشِي عَلَى النَّمَارِقِ recezinde “nemârik” zerâbî mânasına kullanılmıştır.
